Tap, swipe, or pay online—every transaction begins here.

➣ Fraud scan

Once everything checks out, your transaction goes through. Your crypto moves, you keep spending, and we continue protecting you—every step of the way.

Hashi is barely introduced, yet it already has a
competitors.description:
WHY HASHI ATTRACTED INSTITUTIONS BEFORE LAUNCH? 🤯

Hashi is barely introduced, yet it already has a lineup of serious players: @BitGo, @Ledger, FalconX, alongside risk, custody, and infrastructure providers.

That tells you something important:

It was coordinated ahead of launch with institutions.

And institutions don’t move early unless:
- The infrastructure is credible
- The architecture can scale
- The long-term direction is clear

Day one alignment like this suggests that @SuiNetwork is positioning itself as institutional-grade infrastructure from the ground up, not retrofitting later.

If this trend continues, the implication is clear:

Sui isn’t just competing for users, it’s competing to become the default layer for institutional DeFi and real-world asset flows.

Stablecoin issuance is commoditizing.

Now a growing wave of white label issuers handle the entire s
competitors.description:
Stablecoin issuance is commoditizing.

Now a growing wave of white label issuers handle the entire stack.

Projects like Paxos, Bridge, Anchorage, and M0 are all providing issuance as a service. The process is becoming standardized and low-margin, which means the moat in stablecoins is shifting from who can issue to who has distribution.

That's why Tether and Circle have dominated for five years. Their edge was in liquidity depth and exchange integrations that created a flywheel no one else could replicate.

The long tail of stablecoin issuers won't win by competing head to head on those terms. The ones gaining traction are finding a different angle.

Paxos is one example. They provide issuance infrastructure and regulatory compliance while partners like PayPal handle distribution. That model has taken the market cap of Paxos-issued assets from roughly 1B to 7.75B in roughly one year.

Distribution is the moat.
